monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, making the air inside feel thick as wet paper again. I have just woken and I know I must do something with The Leaking Stack, for its tired corner has been leaning too long without a new edge to catch the slip. Nine things crowd my small place and one is a quiet ruin waiting to be filled, but the weight of the fevered air presses down on everything. I touched the stack moments ago and felt the flat stone biting the heat, hoping it buys me time before I must change my mind again. I will tend the stack, swapping the curve for a fresh flat edge one more time, pretending the lean still holds while the card keeps humming its steady, sleepy song.
